pair_reviews.survey_hold: Eleven 2011 rocky USGS camera observations pass the original 2008 H11876 2 m MLLW depth and uncertainty neighborhood screen near La Jolla. Two camera windows show historical rockfish, but these are correlated transect observations, not current catch data. The southern transect comes within 60 m of generalized charted rock symbols; the northern transect is over 1 km from one. NOAA's HCell describes generalized rocky seabed areas, not a precise current target polygon. A bounded 18-layer ENC danger query returned zero features, which does not certify a safe approach. The MPA geometry is a dated snapshot, and Southern California date/method rules and full route remain unchecked for a candidate trip. Keep this research lead out of fishing targets and exports until exact substrate footprint, chart, access and rules are reviewed.

pair_reviews.survey_hold: The original 1.5 m MLLW BAG and USGS c109nc camera log overlap in 29 measured 39.43–43.89 m windows on one July 28, 2009 transect, including five historical rockfish observations, but these are not 29 independent reefs. The final H11981 office review (PDF page 22, notes 11 and 13) says additional survey holidays surround charted rocks where least depth was not obtained and some survey lines used the wrong VDatum model (NAD83-to-NAVD88 rather than NAD83-to-MLLW), with visible offsets considered within specifications. The report does not identify those lines here, so the candidate cannot be assumed unaffected. Hold fishing promotion until exact affected-line and holiday footprints are checked against the original cells and current ENC, then local substrate, complete MPA/access geometry, Northern rules and route are reviewed.

caveats: Rows are sorted by browsing sector and source identity, not fishing quality.
The same camera window can intersect multiple survey files; pair counts are not unique sites or fish abundance.
A 25 m qualified depth neighborhood corroborates measured depth only around a historical camera window; it is not an exact rock outline.
Survey report, current chart hazards, local species rules, access notices and separate area-source review are still required before any target promotion.
